name: Bachíniva, in the corrido
synopsis: In the song the hotel girl sings at Casas Grandes, six armed riders arrive at Bachíniva in April and the fair-haired youth faces them without fear. As she tells the ending, he and his sweetheart die together when their bullets run out, and the townspeople bury them in a hidden place.

name: Galeana
synopsis: According to Quijada, Boyd killed two men here and nobody knows why. Neither even worked for the Babícora, but one of them had a brother who was a friend of the alguacil.

name: San Lorenzo, Chihuahua
synopsis: Quijada says Boyd was killed here, not at Ignacio Zaragoza as Billy has heard. “The girl” was taken away bloodied and stumbling, so many thought she had been shot, but she was not. What became of her Quijada does not know, though he guesses she may have gone home to her family.

name: San Buenaventura
synopsis: Boyd lies buried in the town's cemetery, Billy is told, first by a woman at the Namiquipa wake and then by Quijada. There is no stone, only a board, and Quijada adds that Boyd was much loved by ordinary people.

name: The border at Columbus
synopsis: Billy rides through the gate in rags and insists to the guard that he is American. The guard takes him for a returning recruit, and Billy learns only now that the country has gone to war.

name: Deming at midnight
synopsis: Billy sleeps on the bus station floor with his horse tied to a lamp post outside. In the morning the woman at the cafe feeds him for nothing, he forges a name on the parental consent form, and a doctor hears a heart murmur and turns him away. He takes ten days' work at a stable to pay for clothes and a bus ticket.

name: El Paso, the recruiting office
synopsis: In new clothes, Billy queues naked with the other men for the medical. The army doctor finds the same irregular heartbeat and will not pass him, though he says it is probably not serious. Billy eats lunch at the Splendid Cafe and catches the bus back.

name: Back to Deming
synopsis: Next morning Mr Chandler at the stable asks how it went. Billy says he means to try once more in Albuquerque, works out the week and collects his wages.

name: Past Socorro at nightfall
synopsis: Darkness falls on the bus north of Socorro. From the window Billy watches flocks of waterfowl settle onto the marshes by the river, but the engine drowns out their calls.

name: Albuquerque
synopsis: After a night at the YMCA Billy is rejected a third time. He asks the doctor for some medicine to get him through and says he has no home to return to, but the doctor tells him the rules leave no way round it.

name: Deming at three in the morning
synopsis: The bus gets in before dawn and Billy goes straight to the stable to saddle Niño in the cold. The groom Ruiz watches, asks where he is going, and wishes him a good journey when Billy says he has no idea.

name: Hermanas
synopsis: Riding south on the old road on a freshly shod, grain-fed horse, Billy keeps going from dawn into the dark. He sleeps out on the high plain and is up again shivering before first light.

name: Hachita, leaving the road
synopsis: Billy leaves the road a short way west of Hachita and heads across country.

name: The Little Hatchet foothills
synopsis: Billy crosses the lower slopes of the Little Hatchets and the railway coming up from the Phelps Dodge smelter further south.

name: The shallow salt lake
synopsis: The flooded salt flats glow red in the sunset, and the horse cannot see a far shore and refuses to wade in. Billy turns south along the edge, with snow on Gillespie Mountain and the Animas Peaks, and burns old fence posts for a campfire while telling the horse it has only itself to blame.

name: The old Playas road over the mountains
synopsis: In the morning horse and rider cross the lake after all. Before noon they pick up the old Playas road and follow it west into the mountains, where the snow in the pass is unmarked by any track.

name: Animas
synopsis: Billy comes down out of the mountains into the Animas Valley and takes the southbound road from Animas.

name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
synopsis: Leona lets Billy in and Mr Sanders, frailer than before, asks at once where Boyd is. Over supper he tells Billy that Miller has gone into the army despite his leg, and shows him old photographs, including John Slaughter and Apache May. He talks about cattle days and Villa's raid, but cannot persuade Billy to stay the night.

name: Camp on the Animas Plain
synopsis: Billy sleeps out on the plain under the old man's gift of a blanket while his small fire burns out. Seeing lightning far to the south over Mexico, he feels sure he will end his days far from this valley, and murmurs to himself that nothing in the world is certain.

name: Winslow, paid off from the Hashknife linecamp
synopsis: After three lonely months at a linecamp, Billy collects his pay in March and posts Mr Sanders the twenty dollars he owes. In the first bar he is refused a beer. In the second a drunk soldier needles him and the barman talks about the war until Billy drains his glass and leaves.

name: Magdalena
synopsis: Nine more months on, Billy rides south with a traded packhorse, a proper bedroll and an old single-shot Stevens rifle. His route takes him through Magdalena.

name: The plains of San Agustín
synopsis: Billy rides south across these high plains, which the book calls Saint Augustine.

name: Silver City, Christmas
synopsis: Billy rides in through snow, takes a room at the Palace Hotel and, with the feed store shut, feeds the horses boxed cereal from a grocery. Next morning every shop is closed, and the clerk tells him it is Christmas Day.

name: A small ranch out of Magdalena
synopsis: Billy works for the Matadors and the T Diamond in the Texas panhandle, then on small spreads for a week here and there. By the war's third spring gold stars hang in nearly every ranch window. He stays on a little ranch near Magdalena until March, then draws his pay and heads south.

name: East of Steins, the last blacktop
synopsis: Riding south with his packhorse, Billy crosses the last paved road he will meet, a little east of Steins.

name: The SK Bar gate
synopsis: Mr Sanders, his eyes poor since a cataract operation, tells Billy from his porch that Miller was killed on Kwajalein and that Leona has married and moved away. Billy admits he has heard nothing of Boyd and is talked into supper as rain threatens. At dawn the Mexican cook serves him breakfast, and when he asks her to pray for him she says she already meant to.

name: Mexican customs at Berendo
synopsis: Billy tips the customs officer a silver dollar for the stamped papers on his horses. He last came this way at thirteen to collect a herd of cattle, when his father rode the horse Billy rides now. The cafe is gone, so he buys tacos at a roadside brazier and eats them in the saddle.

name: Janos
synopsis: Billy looks west to the Pilares from the old road, then rides into the ruined mud town and follows music to a cantina. He buys whiskey for the men there, flings away the drink of a drunk revolutionary veteran, Alfonso, and says he has come to find his brother. He spits out the mescal Alfonso pours him, turns when called to face his bared bullet scars, and walks out unharmed.

name: Casas Grandes
synopsis: He passes through the town in the evening and turns south on the road he first rode with Boyd three years earlier. In the dusk he goes by the old ruins and ballcourts, where nighthawks are still out hunting.

name: San Diego, on the road south
synopsis: Next day he crosses the plank bridge to the hacienda and finds the Muñoz house stripped bare, with only old candle drippings where the Virgin used to stand. An old man making baskets in the courtyard says the family have gone but cannot say where.

name: Las Varas
synopsis: Two days later he rides through Las Varas and turns east for La Boquilla, along the road where he and Boyd once saw their father's horse climb dripping out of the lake.

name: Camp on the plain by the lake, the red plane
synopsis: A dry north wind lifts so much dust off Babícora, beyond the lake, that it looks like smoke from a fire. At dusk a big red Waco plane flies in from the west and lands among the trees, and he camps on the open plain, where the wind devours his small fire.

name: Babícora
synopsis: He rides through Babícora the next day on his way towards Namiquipa.

name: Santa Ana de Babícora
synopsis: He rides through the village the same day and takes the road north to Namiquipa.

name: Namiquipa, now a mining camp
synopsis: He stakes the horses in willows by the river below the town, then bathes and washes his clothes. In the morning a bride in a mule cart crosses herself at the sight of him. In the empty streets a door he knocks on swings open on an old man laid out for burial, and Billy leaves with a yellow flower from beside the body.

name: Temósachic
synopsis: After weeks of asking after “the girl” across that country, he hears verses of a corrido about a fair-haired young man from the north in a bodega here. The singer tells him only that the youth wanted justice and has been dead for years.

name: Madera, the late April fair
synopsis: At a fair by the railway in this cold sawmill town, a shill hands him a card that wins the lotería wheel and a free look inside a painted caravan. Billy knows it as the old opera company's wagon from the hacienda at San Diego, refuses to go in, and rides off south for Temósachic.

name: Babícora before dawn
synopsis: A week later he rides through the silent town by moonlight and follows the newly graded road north. He sleeps by a ciénega in a ring of old cottonwoods and wakes to find a rider he knows from before watching him. The man asks after “the girl”, talks at length about death and fate, and rides off, leaving Billy to check his pistol.

name: Casas Grandes, the Camino Recto hotel
synopsis: He takes a room at the hotel on 15 May, a date he learns from the first newspaper he has seen in seven weeks. Next morning a girl of about sixteen sits cracking pecans in the courtyard and singing a corrido. She knows only a little of it, and before he goes back upstairs she presses a handful of the nuts into his hand.

name: The high country of the Babícora
synopsis: For days he rides these uplands, hiding small fires in sheltered hollows and lying out at night under the stars. Walking back to the fire he often thinks of Boyd. He watches parties of vaqueros, some on mules, cross the high grass and drive cattle through the passes, but never goes near their fires.

name: Quijada's cabin
synopsis: Riding west towards a gap at sunset, he finds a lone lit cabin. It belongs to Quijada, the Yaqui manager who once let him and Boyd take back their horses, and over coffee he confirms that Boyd is dead and buried at San Buenaventura. When Billy says he means to take his brother home, Quijada warns him nobody will allow it.

name: San Buenaventura
synopsis: He rides in through the puddles past the whitewashed trees of the alameda and the church, and goes out to find the cemetery. Back after dark, he asks an old woman praying alone in the church about the gravedigger and the priest. One has died and the other has left, and she promises to pray for him.

name: The cemetery on the Gallego road
synopsis: Against the south wall he finds a nameless board cross dated February 1943, left by Boyd's comrades. Next day he digs all day, and when he tries to haul the coffin out with his horse it breaks apart. By torchlight he lifts the light bones out, wraps them in his bedroll, refills the grave near midnight, and takes the cross with him.

name: Past the lights of Casas Grandes, to the west
synopsis: Leading the packhorse with Boyd's remains, he crosses the highway and goes cross-country by night, keeping the North Star on his right. On the second night he sees the town's lights off to the west and leaves them behind.

name: The Casas Grandes River, across the Guzmán road
synopsis: He crosses the old road from Guzmán and Sabinal, reaches the river and turns north up the trail along its bank.

name: Corralitos before dawn
synopsis: He rides through the half-ruined town before daylight, past houses cut with loopholes from the Apache days and dark heaps of mine slag, and crosses the railway.

name: The river trail north of Corralitos
synopsis: One of four riders who stop him at dawn slashes open the bundle of bones, stabs Niño in the chest and takes Billy's pistol. Billy stops the bleeding with river clay and loses the packhorse. Next morning gypsies from Durango, hauling an old airplane north by oxen, tell him its story while a herbal brew boils, then pour it into Niño and poultice the wound.

name: The border, west of Dog Springs
synopsis: Three days after setting out with Boyd's remains on a travois, Billy reaches the line and rides past the first white boundary obelisk. He drags the poles across the cracked floor of an old dry reservoir printed with the tracks of cattle, antelope, coyotes and cranes. That night, back in the United States, he dreams of silent travellers at dusk, coming back from some labour he cannot make out.

name: Hermanas
synopsis: The next day Billy rides through Hermanas and on along the dirt road westward, still hauling the travois.

name: Hachita, the crossroads store
synopsis: At evening Billy halts his horse where the roads cross by the store. He gazes south-west at the Animas Peaks in the last sunlight, sure that he will not return to them.

name: Animas, Ash Wednesday
synopsis: After a whole day dragging the travois slowly across the Animas Valley, Billy enters the town on the morning of Ash Wednesday. A Mexican woman and five children with ash on their foreheads cross themselves at the sight of the body and walk on without returning his greeting.

name: The little cemetery south of Animas
synopsis: With a spade from the town's hardware store, Billy hobbles his horse outside a small cemetery and digs a grave for Boyd. He is waist deep in caliche when the sheriff arrives, guesses who he is, and says a man may not bury his dead just anywhere. He will try to get a death certificate from the judge, and Billy must report to him in Lordsburg next day.

name: Silver City
synopsis: In the days after Animas, Billy rides north to Silver City.

name: Duncan, Arizona
synopsis: From Silver City Billy turns west and crosses into Arizona at Duncan.

name: Glenwood
synopsis: Billy turns north once more and crosses the mountains to Glenwood.

name: Reserve
synopsis: Billy rides on to Reserve. For a time he has work with the Carrizozos and with the GS outfit, and he quits them both, unable to say why.

name: Silver City, July
synopsis: In July Billy drifts back south to Silver City and from there sets off east along the old road.

name: The Santa Rita mines
synopsis: Riding east on the old road, Billy passes the Santa Rita mines.

name: San Lorenzo, New Mexico
synopsis: Billy rides through San Lorenzo, still following the old road east towards the Black Range.

name: Over the Black Range
synopsis: Billy crosses the Black Range on the old road. Past it the weather turns, with a wind from the northern mountains and cloud shadow spreading over the plain ahead. His horse plods with its head low while he sits upright in the saddle, hat down over his eyes.

name: The ruined waystation by the blacktop
synopsis: Crossing a fenceless plain of catclaw and creosote, Billy reaches the blacktop and turns back in the rain to three adobes, nearly roofless, that were once a waystation. He beds down in the hay, but a crippled, half-blind old yellow dog limps in, and he drives it out with rocks and a length of pipe until it hobbles away howling up the road.
